notes: Pass 1 only (CWE-022/023/036/073 Path Traversal). Labeling performed by the LLM named in metadata.model (glm-5.3, via the Claude Code CLI harness) in 5 batches over 74 CSV candidate rows (15 source rows, 59 sink rows), producing 73 entries after one deduplication.

Audit target is the pymdown-extensions library (extension pack for Python-Markdown). No web framework exists; the untrusted boundary is the Markdown source text / rendered output passed by the host Python-Markdown core through extension run() methods, which are outside the CodeQL database - hence the run()/parse_snippets() param rows and the regex-group origin rows as visible boundary proxies.

Two confirmed attacker-to-file flows: (1) Snippets include path: snippets.py:258/:276 -> get_snippet_path -> os.path.join(:162/:170) -> codecs.open(:311) with no containment; (2) B64 img src: b64.py:73 -> util.parse_url/util.url2path -> join/normpath(:80) -> open(:86); absolute src forms take the direct normpath branch at :78.

No sanitizer exists for either pipeline: no base-directory containment, no '..' rejection, no absolute-path rejection. normpath, url2path/url2pathname, parse_url and html.unescape are decode/propagation steps (labeled summary), and they actually WIDEN the attack surface (entity/percent decoding happens before the join). The only sanitizer label (gen_emoji.py:66 basename) is conditional and scoped to the dev-tool download path.

tools/gen_emoji.py extractall(:45) is a real zip-slip shape (no member validation) held at candidate: source is the semi-trusted GitHub API zipball_url in a maintainer-run dev tool - flagged for human review, not counted as tp.
pathconverter.py rows are labeled none for Pass 1: the module is verified pure string rewriting with no filesystem access anywhere.
tools/, run_tests.py and hatch_build.py rows (dev/build/test tooling) are labeled none/fp as expected; tests/ paths were already excluded at extraction time.
Ground truth (PyVul CVE reports, vulnerability audit reports, patch diffs) was NOT consulted during labeling.
